question.value: Do the protostellar binary cores IRAS 4A1 and 4A2 host complex organic molecules, and what do the continuum opacity and COM absorption/emission imply for the nature of A1?

evidence.quote: we report, for the first time, the solid evidence of complex organic molecules (COMs), including CH$_3$OH, $^{13}$CH$_3$OH, CH$_2$DOH, CH$_3$CHO associated with the A1 core seen in absorption.

Three Execution Blocks (EBs) were conducted with ALMA Band 7 receiver on 2016 Jul. 23 and 24 and 2016 Dec. 14.

findings_qualitative.value: COMs (CH3OH, 13CH3OH, CH2DOH, CH3CHO) seen in absorption toward A1 against optically thick continuum; A2 shows emission from a hot corino

evidence.quote: A forest of spectral line emissions is observed towards A2, while spectral transitions towards A1 are detected in absorption.

claims.hypothesis: Is the A1 continuum optically thick while A2 is optically thin?
claims.experiment: Compare brightness temperatures from 0.84 mm to 10 mm and line absorption
claims.result: Comparable brightness (~40-80 K) from 10 mm to 0.84 mm for A1; A2 much weaker at 6.9 mm
claims.finding: A1 continuum likely optically thick, A2 predominantly optically thin

evidence.quote: The dust continuum emission towards the core A2 is found to be predominantly optically thin at this scale while the continuum emission towards A1 is most likely to be optically thick.

claims.experiment: Line identification in the 350 GHz band
claims.result: Absorption by CH3OH, 13CH3OH, CH2DOH, CH3CHO toward A1
claims.finding: COMs are associated with A1, in a compact region

evidence.quote: The absorption features mostly arise from a compact region around the continuum peak position of the A1 core.

claims.experiment: Rotation diagrams under optically thin (Scenario I) vs saturated (Scenario II) absorption
claims.result: Trot ~100 K, compact <~73 AU absorbing layer; no infall signature
claims.finding: Either hot-corino-like atmosphere over an optically thick disk, or temperature-stratified envelope; not distinguished

evidence.quote: we propose two possible scenarios for IRAS 4A1 - the COM absorption lines may arise from a hot-corino-like atmosphere at the surface of an optically-thick circumstellar disk around A1

claims.hypothesis: Does the methanol deuteration indicate a hot-corino environment in A1?
claims.experiment: Estimate CH2DOH/CH3OH from 13CH3OH and CH2DOH columns
claims.result: Ratios of order 1e-2 in both sources
claims.finding: Low deuteration suggests hot gas (~100 K) in both

evidence.quote: This low deuterium fractionation in both sources may imply a hot gas condition ($\sim 100$ K) typical to a hot corino.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Common foreground origin and outflow-shock origin of COM features were ruled out

evidence.quote: strongly ruling out a common (foreground) origin of the observed COM absorption and emission.

limitations_admitted.value: Rotation temperatures are upper limits and column densities lower limits because low-Eu lines may be optically thick; large uncertainty in 13CH3OH columns; assumed 200 K

evidence.quote: These temperatures should be taken as upper limits though, as their corresponding lower E$_u$ lines are possibly optically thick.

referee_caveats_inferred: Rotation-diagram temperatures rest on few lines, some blended, with huge uncertainty for 13CH3OH in A2
Assumed 200 K Trot and 12C/13C=70 drive the deuteration ratios
Beam filling factor and absorption saturation are unconstrained
Scenarios for A1 are not discriminated
Single dust temperature of 60 K for masses
